message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Laurasiatheria is a major group of placental mammals that includes the orders Carnivora (to which lions belong) and Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong), among others. Thus, the most recent common ancestor shared by lions and zebras lived before the divergence of these two orders but after the split of Laurasiatheria from the other placental mammal lineages.
